c.tagline: Home of Disneyland, sunshine, and Orange County's biggest stage.

taxi.fareNote: Metered street taxis exist but ride-hailing apps (Uber/Lyft) are far more common and usually cheaper for visitors.

emergency.note: 911 is the single nationwide emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Keep valuables out of sight in parked cars and watch for petty theft in busy parking lots and motel strips away from the resort district.

hood_desc: The tourist heart surrounding Disneyland Park and Disney California Adventure, with the Downtown Disney District, palm-lined Harbor Boulevard, and hotels of every price within walking distance of the parks.
The area around the Anaheim Convention Center, the largest on the West Coast, lined with big full-service convention hotels on Katella Avenue just south of the Disney resort.
The stadium district between Angel Stadium and the Honda Center, home to Anaheim's ARTIC transit hub and a growing cluster of apartments and hotels near Metrolink and Amtrak service.
lodging: TownePlace Suites by Marriott Anaheim Maingate Near Angel Stadium

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though many locals prefer bottled or filtered for taste.

transit.hours: OCTA buses run roughly 5am to 11pm; ART resort shuttles run from early morning to after the parks close; Metrolink trains run mainly daytime and early evening.
transit.note: Anaheim is car-oriented, but OCTA buses cover Orange County, the ART trolley loops the resort and convention area, and Metrolink and Amtrak connect the ARTIC hub to Los Angeles and the wider region.
transit.pay: Pay OCTA bus fares ($2 per ride) with cash or the OC Bus app; the ART resort shuttle uses its own day passes bought online or at the ARTIC hub and kiosks.

train: Anaheim Regional Transportation Intermodal Center (ARTIC) - Amtrak/Metrolink

transit.m: OCTA Route 43 bus toward Anaheim (~50 min, with connection)
Taxi or rideshare to the Disney resort (20-30 min)

tip.r: ~15-20% at sit-down restaurants is expected; round up or ~15% for taxis and bar service.

food.name: Mesquite-grilled tacos
food.desc: Orange County Mexican-American cooking at its best: carne asada and al pastor grilled over mesquite, folded into small corn tortillas with salsa.

places.name: Tacos Los Cholos
places.note: Cult mesquite-grill taqueria; tight parking but consistently the city's best tacos.

places.name: Los Sanchez Restaurant
places.note: Long-standing family Mexican kitchen popular with locals rather than tourists.

places.name: Anaheim Packing House
places.note: 1919 citrus warehouse turned food hall with several taco and Mexican stalls.

food.name: Mandi and whole roast lamb
food.desc: Yemeni feast food: lamb, chicken or fish slow-roasted and piled on fragrant spiced rice, ordered on platters built to feed a whole table.

places.name: House of Mandi
places.note: Community tentpole on Brookhurst with mandi platters sized for 3 to 18 people.

places.name: Little Arabia Lebanese Bakery
places.note: Compact Levantine kitchen and bakery serving roasts, rice dishes and pastries.

places.name: Brookhurst Street restaurants
places.note: The largest Middle Eastern restaurant strip on the West Coast, worth grazing.

food.name: Manaeesh
food.desc: Levantine flatbread baked to order and topped with zaatar and olive oil, cheese, spiced lamb, or labneh with honey; eaten hot from the oven.

places.name: Forn Al Hara
places.note: Lebanese bakery whose stone oven turns out manaeesh through the morning.

places.name: Little Arabia Lebanese Bakery
places.note: Bakery and cafe open since 2014, good for flatbreads and sweets to go.

places.name: Brookhurst Street bakeries
places.note: Several Arab bakeries within a few blocks sell manaeesh, knafeh and baklava.

food.name: Falafel, shawarma and mezze
food.desc: Crisp falafel, shaved shawarma, hummus, baba ghanoush and tabbouleh - the everyday Levantine spread that defines Anaheim's Little Arabia.

places.name: Sahara Falafel
places.note: Neighbourhood standard for falafel, shawarma wraps and hummus plates.

places.name: Kareem's Falafel
places.note: Long-running counter shop on Brookhurst with a devoted local following.

places.name: Little Arabia Lebanese Bakery
places.note: Small dining room turning out mezze alongside its bakery counter.

food.name: Pho and banh mi
food.desc: Little Saigon sits minutes south of Anaheim: beef pho, grilled-pork rice plates, nem nuong rolls and crackling baguette banh mi.

places.name: Brodard
places.note: Famous for nem nuong cuon grilled-pork rolls and their addictive dipping sauce.

places.name: Pho 79
places.note: James Beard-recognised pho house, one of the oldest in Little Saigon.

places.name: Banh Mi Che Cali
places.note: Bustling bakery counter for cheap, freshly baked banh mi and che desserts.

food.name: Theme-park classics
food.desc: Anaheim's own institutions: the deep-fried Monte Cristo sandwich, hand-dipped corn dogs, and pineapple Dole Whip soft serve.

places.name: Blue Bayou
places.note: Bayou-lit dining room inside Pirates of the Caribbean, home of the Monte Cristo.

places.name: Carnation Cafe
places.note: The park's oldest restaurant, serving American diner classics since 1955.

places.name: Anaheim Packing House
places.note: Food hall alternative for corn dogs, ice cream and local snacks off-park.

food.name: Anaheim craft beer
food.desc: The city was founded by German winemakers and now brews hard: revived heritage lagers plus hazy IPAs from a tight cluster of taprooms.

places.name: Anaheim Brewery
places.note: Revival of the original 1870s city brewery, pouring German-style lagers.

places.name: Noble Ale Works
places.note: Award-winning taproom near the stadium, known for its hoppy ales.

places.name: Unsung Brewing
places.note: Comic-book themed downtown brewery with a rotating taproom line-up.

food.name: Horchata and mint lemonade
food.desc: Two neighbourhood staples: cinnamon-rice horchata and fruit aguas frescas from the taquerias, and blended mint lemonade from Little Arabia.

places.name: Tacos Los Cholos
places.note: House horchata and aguas frescas to wash down the mesquite-grilled tacos.

places.name: Little Arabia Lebanese Bakery
places.note: Icy blended mint lemonade, the standard Levantine warm-weather drink.

places.name: Anaheim Packing House
places.note: Food-hall stalls pour aguas frescas, juices and coffee under one roof.

landmarks: Sleeping Beauty Castle (Disneyland)
The fairy-tale centerpiece of Disneyland Park and one of the most photographed castles in the world.
Matterhorn Bobsleds
Disneyland's iconic snow-capped mountain attraction, a towering landmark visible throughout the park.
Downtown Disney District
A lively outdoor promenade of shops, restaurants, and entertainment linking Disneyland's two theme parks.
Pixar Pier (Disney California Adventure)
A colorful boardwalk-style waterfront area with the iconic Incredicoaster and a lagoon perfect for sunset photos.
Angel Stadium of Anaheim
The historic home of the Los Angeles Angels, famous for its towering "Big A" sign and rocky outfield display.
Honda Center
Anaheim's distinctive arched-roof sports and concert arena, home to the Anaheim Ducks.
Anaheim Packing House
A beautifully restored 1919 citrus-packing plant turned bustling gourmet food hall with striking industrial architecture.
Center Street Promenade
A pedestrian-friendly stretch in downtown Anaheim lined with murals, cafes, and local color.
Anaheim Convention Center
The largest convention center on the West Coast, an architectural landmark and home to major expos like D23.
MUZEO Anaheim
A striking Carnegie-library-turned-museum showcasing rotating exhibits on art, history, and culture.

train.note: Trains use ARTIC, the Anaheim Regional Transportation Intermodal Center beside Angel Stadium and the Honda Center, about two miles from Disneyland and linked to the resort by Anaheim Resort Transportation shuttles. Amtrak's Pacific Surfliner calls around 13 times a day in each direction between San Diego, Los Angeles and Santa Barbara, and Metrolink's Orange County Line adds weekday commuter runs toward Los Angeles and Oceanside. No international passenger train serves the US West Coast at all - for Mexico you ride the Surfliner to San Diego, take the trolley to San Ysidro and cross to Tijuana on foot. Surfliner fares are cheapest booked a few days ahead on Amtrak's own site.

intl.to: Tijuana & northern Mexico (Mexico) - change in Los Angeles or San Diego

bus.note: Greyhound, FlixBus, Megabus and the Mexican carrier Tres Estrellas de Oro all use the bus bays at ARTIC, so coaches and trains share one building. Cross-border services generally require a connection in Los Angeles or San Diego rather than running through from Anaheim; carry your passport and check US re-entry documents for the return. FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/) and Megabus (https://us.megabus.com/) handle most of the cheap runs up to Los Angeles (about an hour) and down to San Diego (about two hours). Tickets are bought online; there is no full ticket counter for every operator at ARTIC.

intl.to: Avalon, Santa Catalina Island (USA) - departs Dana Point Harbor, about 35 min south of Anaheim, also San Pedro and Long Beach
Avalon, Santa Catalina Island (USA) - departs Newport Beach, about 20 miles south

ferry.note: Anaheim is inland, so every boat leaves from an Orange County or Los Angeles port you have to drive or ride to. Catalina Express crosses from Dana Point, Long Beach or San Pedro to Avalon in about 60-90 minutes and runs year round; the 600-passenger Catalina Flyer catamaran does the Newport Beach to Avalon run in roughly 75 minutes. Sailings fill on summer weekends and holidays, so book ahead. There are no international ferries anywhere on this stretch of coast.

half.name: Huntington Beach
half.blurb: Long Orange County surf beach with a historic pier, known as Surf City USA.

half.name: Laguna Beach
half.blurb: Clifftop coastal town with coves, tide pools, and a well-known art gallery scene.

full.name: Catalina Island
full.blurb: Small resort island off the coast reached by high-speed ferry, with snorkeling and a Mediterranean-style harbor town.

full.name: Joshua Tree National Park
full.blurb: Desert park where two ecosystems meet, filled with twisted namesake trees and giant boulder formations.
